Webb were accompanied by a volume of 94 pages, containing the most absurd statements as to the action of the Philadelphia Brigade at the Battle of Gettysburg, which, upon being read, led to the unanimous adoption of the following preamble and resolution:

70290-the-adventures-of-hatim-tai-a-roma.title: Revised And Edited, With Introduction
70290-the-adventures-of-hatim-tai-a-roma.creator: William Rounseville Alger
70290-the-adventures-of-hatim-tai-a-roma.description: A book by William Rounseville Alger. In exciting interest, in ethical charm, in imaginative richness of startling adventures, it is not one whit inferior to the very best of those world-renowned masterpieces. It is a magnificent specimen of that ideal freedom of genius which creates its own world, peoples it with its own productions and events, and sympathizes, in vivid interior reproduction, with the romantic experiences of its characters and their destinies.

arxiv-2002-03110.title: Entropy and Mass Distribution in Disc Galaxies
arxiv-2002-03110.creator: John Herbert Marr
arxiv-2002-03110.description: Abstract The relaxed motion of stars and gas in galactic discs is well approximated by a rotational velocity that is a function of radial position only, implying that individual components have lost any information about their prior states. Thermodynamically, such an equilibrium state is a microcanonical ensemble with maximum entropy, characterised by a lognormal probability distribution.

arxiv-2107-01251.title: Uncertainty in Lung Cancer Stage for Outcome Estimation via Set-Valued Classification Publication type: Article Type
arxiv-2107-01251.creator: Savannah Bergquist*, Gabriel Brooks, Mary Beth Landrum, Nancy Keating, Sherri Rose
arxiv-2107-01251.description: Abstract Difficulty in identifying cancer stage in health care claims data has limited oncology quality of care and health outcomes research. We fit prediction algorithms for classifying lung cancer stage into three classes (stages I/II, stage III, and stage IV) using claims data, and then demonstrate a method for incorporating the classification uncertainty in outcomes estimation.

arxiv-2210-01546.title: An RNA Sequencing Analysis of Glaucoma Genesis in Mice
arxiv-2210-01546.creator: Jai Sharma, Vidhyacharan Bhaskar
arxiv-2210-01546.description: Abstract Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness in people over the age of 60, accounting for 6.6 to 8% of all blindness in 2010, but there is still much to be learned about the genetic origins of the eye disease.

arxiv-2212-12478.title: Image Classification with Small Datasets: Overview and Benchmark
arxiv-2212-12478.creator: LORENZO BRIGATO 1, BJÖRN BARZ 2, LUCA IOCCHI 1, AND JOACHIM DENZLER 2
arxiv-2212-12478.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by LORENZO BRIGATO 1, BJÖRN BARZ 2, LUCA IOCCHI 1, AND JOACHIM DENZLER 2. Image classification with small datasets has been an active research area in the recent past. However, as research in this scope is still in its infancy, two key ingredients are missing for ensuring reliable and truthful progress: a systematic and extensive overview of the state of the art, and a common benchmark to allow for objective comparisons between published methods. This article addresses both issues.

arxiv-2311-16270.title: Initial Characterization of the First Speedster-EXD550 Event-Driven X-Ray Hybrid Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor Detectors
arxiv-2311-16270.creator: Joseph M. Colosimo, Hannah M. Grzybowski, Evan C. Jennerjahn, Lukas R. Stone, Abraham D. Falcone, Mitchell Wages, Jacob C. Buffington, David N. Burrows, Zachary E. Catlin, Timothy Emeigh, Fredric Hancock
arxiv-2311-16270.description: Abstract Future x-ray observatories will require imaging detectors with fast readout speeds that simultaneously achieve or exceed the other high performance parameters of x-ray charge-coupled devices (CCDs) used in many missions over the past three decades. Fast readout will reduce the impact of pile-up in missions with large collecting areas while also improving performance in other respects like timing resolution.

arxiv-2402-13739.title: Hidden Gems in the Rough: Computational Notebooks as an Uncharted Oasis for IDEs CCS: Software and its engineering Development frameworks and environments
arxiv-2402-13739.creator: Sergey Titov, Konstantin Grotov, Ashwin Prasad S. Venkatesh
arxiv-2402-13739.description: Abstract . In this paper, we outline potential ways for the further development of computational notebooks in Integrated Development Environments (IDEs). We discuss notebooks integration with IDEs, focusing on three main areas: facilitating experimentation, adding collaborative features, and improving code comprehension.

arxiv-2405-11983.title: A review on the use of large language models as virtual tutors
arxiv-2405-11983.creator: Silvia García-Méndez, Francisco de Arriba-Pérez, María del Carmen Somoza-López
arxiv-2405-11983.description: Abstract Transformer architectures contribute to managing long-term dependencies for Natural Language Processing, representing one of the most recent changes in the field. These architectures are the basis of the innovative, cutting-edge Large Language Models ( llm s) that have produced a huge buzz in several fields and industrial sectors, among the ones education stands out.

arxiv-2406-17106.title: Purely vision-based collective movement of robots
arxiv-2406-17106.creator: David Mezey 1 , 2 ∗ {}^{1,2^{*}} , Renaud Bastien 3 , Yating Zheng 1,2 , Neal McKee 5 , David Stoll 2 , Heiko Hamann 2 , 4 ∗ ⁣ ∗ {}^{2,4^{**}} & Pawel Romanczuk 1,
arxiv-2406-17106.description: Abstract Collective movement inspired by animal groups promises inherited benefits for robot swarms, such as enhanced sensing and efficiency. However, while animals move in groups using only their local senses, robots often obey central control or use direct communication, introducing systemic weaknesses to the swarm.

arxiv-2412-16230.title: A Sophisticated Analytical Methodology for Refining the Smagorinsky Model in Turbulent Flows
arxiv-2412-16230.creator: Rômulo Damasclin Chaves dos Santos
arxiv-2412-16230.description: Abstract In this work, we present three important theorems related to the corrected Smagorinsky model for turbulence in time-dependent domains. The first theorem establishes an improved regularity criterion for the solution of the corrected Smagorinsky model in Sobolev spaces H s ​ ( Ω ​ ( t ) ) H^{s}(\Omega(t)) with smooth and evolving boundaries.

arxiv-2506-06237.title: Fermion parity switches imprinted in the photonic field of cavity embedded Kitaev chains
arxiv-2506-06237.creator: Victor Fernandez Becerra, Olesia Dmytruk
arxiv-2506-06237.description: Abstract The entanglement of electronic states with quantum light in cavity embedded systems has opened new avenues to manipulate quantum materials. In this work we investigate the Kitaev chain coupled to a single mode photonic cavity. Using exact diagonalization we calculate the many-body energy spectrum of the electron-photon Hamiltonian in finite-length chains.

doe-osti-3366785-small-nuclear-reactors-.title: Small Nuclear Reactors for Maritime Ports
doe-osti-3366785-small-nuclear-reactors-.creator: Whitley, Jeriah A., Calkins, Ryan A., Carpenter-Graffy, Dina E.
doe-osti-3366785-small-nuclear-reactors-.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. Maritime ports are entering a period of sharply rising electricity demand as operations are electrified, shore power adoption grows, and energy-intensive industries expand near ports. This report evaluates the feasibility of small nuclear reactors at U.S. ports, which could offer

pmc-10597028.title: Daily temperature variability in cities and mental health-related hospitalizations
pmc-10597028.creator: G Cohen Shimonovich, S T Rowland, J Benavides, J Lindert, M A Kioumourtzoglou, R M Parks
pmc-10597028.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Despite plausible behavioral and physiological pathways, limited evidence exists on how temperature variability is associated with acute mental health-related episodes. This analysis explored associations between daily temperature range (DTR) and mental health-related hospitalizations in New York State during 1995-2014. A case-crossover design with distributed lag non-linear DTR terms (0-6 days) estimated associations between ZIP Code-level DTR and hospitalizations for mood, anxiety, adjustment, and schizophrenia disorders, adjusting for daily mean temperature, and how associations varied by age, sex, admission type and season.

pmc-10660737.title: Real-Life Use of Component-Specific IgE in IgE-Mediated Cow’s Milk Protein Allergy in a Spanish Paediatric Allergy Centre
pmc-10660737.creator: Caoimhe Cronin, Cristina Muñoz Archidona, Beatriz Fernández Prudencio, Aoife Gallagher, Roberto Velasco Zuniga, Juan Trujillo Wurttele, Marie-Paule Lefranc, James M McDonnell
pmc-10660737.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: In Spain, IgE-mediated cow’s milk protein allergy (CMPA) affects approximately 0.69% of infants. Molecular diagnosis may be useful for monitoring natural spontaneous tolerance development in CMPA. The aim of this study was to retrospectively analyse a cohort of paediatric patients with IgE-mediated CMPA who were avoiding milk products awaiting natural tolerance and determine the relationship between disease persistence and major cow’s milk allergens. Methods: A retrospective chart review of 200 patients diagnosed with IgE-mediated CMPA between 2011 and 2020 was conducted.

pmc-11406309.title: Nurse experiences and perspectives with missed nursing care during COVID‐19: A qualitative study
pmc-11406309.creator: Monica Rochman, Austin Mount‐Campbell, Catherine Shull Fernald
pmc-11406309.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). AimThis study aimed to determine clinical nurse and nurse manager perspectives on missed nursing care (MNC) during the COVID‐19 pandemic.DesignThis study utilized a qualitative exploratory descriptive design.MethodsData were obtained through focus groups and virtual interviews. Purposive sampling was used to select nurse and nurse manager participants in COVID‐19 units and the Emergency Department in one large healthcare organization in the northeastern United States of America.ResultsA total of 15 nurses and nurse managers participated in the study.

pmc-11583554.title: The role of government assistance, housing, and employment on postpartum maternal health across income and race: a mixed methods study
pmc-11583554.creator: Chelsea L. Kracht, Kelsey O. Goynes, Madison Dickey, Briasha Jones, Emerson Simeon, Jada Butler, Maryam Kebbe, Kaja Falkenhain, Emily W. Harville, Elizabeth F. Sutton, Leanne M. Redman
pmc-11583554.description: BackgroundStressful large-scale events, such as the COVID-19 pandemic and natural disasters, impact birthing individuals’ postpartum experiences and their mental health. Resultant changes in government assistance, housing, and employment may further exacerbate these impacts, with differences experienced by varying income levels and races.

pmc-11650784.title: Changes in retail cigarette price after tax increase: Findings from the 2018–2020 ITC Vietnam surveys
pmc-11650784.creator: Thi Phuong Thao Tran, Thi Ngoc Phuong Nguyen, Thu Trang Vu, Thai Uyen Tran, Don Nguyen, Thi Hai Phan, Son Dao The, Min Kyung Lim, Anne C. K. Quah, Jin-Kyoung Oh, Hoang Van Minh
pmc-11650784.description: INTRODUCTIONNo longitudinal study has investigated the impact of cigarette tax increases on retail prices in Vietnam. This study aims to describe changes in the purchase price of cigarettes following an excise tax increase from 70% to 75% in January 2019.

pmc-11716873.title: Machine‐learning analysis of real‐world multimodal data collected autonomously at home detects dementia as precisely as a traditional composite scale
pmc-11716873.creator: Laura M Rueda‐Delgado, Alison R Buick, Hugh Nolan, James B Rowe, Brian Murphy
pmc-11716873.description: BackgroundCurrent tools for Alzheimer's disease screening and staging used in clinical research (e.g. ACE‐3, ADAS‐Cog) require substantial face‐to‐face time with trained professionals, and may be affected by subjectivity, "white coat syndrome" and other biases. Alzheimer's symptomology is multi‐factorial and varies day‐to‐day.

pmc-12370984.title: Membrane Charge Primes the Necroptotic Kinase RIPK3 for Amyloid Assembly
pmc-12370984.creator: Fátima C. Escobedo-González, Andrea Gelardo, Alexandra Reimers, Paula Polonio, Miguel Mompeán, Gustavo A. Titaux-Delgado
pmc-12370984.description: Receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) drives necroptosis by assembling into functional amyloid fibrils. Here we show that lipids modulate RIPK3 amyloidogenesis by stabilizing an aggregation-prone intermediate. While electrostatic repulsion maintains RIPK3 in a soluble state, charge compensation alone is not sufficient for fibril formation and hydrophobic contacts are required to initiate nucleation.

pmc-12579992.title: Assessment and Management of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: From the Perspective of a Physiatrist
pmc-12579992.creator: Yang-Chin Su, Chi-Kuang Feng, Tsui-Fen Yang
pmc-12579992.description: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most encountered spinal deformity in growing children, which may bring significant impacts on patients’ physical function, appearance, and overall quality of life. A physiatrist plays a crucial role in the early diagnosis of AIS and longitudinal management through continuous care.

pmc-12597035.title: Multi-tissue spatial transcriptomics identified simultaneous responses to oxidative stress and apoptosis in parallel with tissue-specific reprogramming in modeled chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder
pmc-12597035.creator: Lainey M Hibbard, Sheng Liu, Yamil G Marambio, Kayleigh N Jennings, Steven S Welc, Jun Wan, Kenneth E White
pmc-12597035.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Musculoskeletal dysfunction in chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD) is associated with morbidity and mortality. Disease alterations in bone and muscle, and among muscle fiber types, have largely been tested by candidate gene analysis in individual tissues. We undertook a multi-tissue spatial transcriptomics (ST) approach to identify and differentiate tissue-specific and -common genomic reprogramming occurring simultaneously in cortical bone, muscle, and marrow during CKD-MBD.

pmc-12754894.title: Unmasking pandemic patterns: decoding the COVID-19’s impact on mortality in Italy with Generalized Gamma overdispersion model
pmc-12754894.creator: Danila Azzolina, Rosanna Comoretto, Daniela Ferrante, Corrado Magnani, Dario Gregori
pmc-12754894.description: BackgroundItaly has been significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in its early stages, resulting in healthcare strain, societal restrictions, and disruption. Understanding the long-term effects, notably excess mortality beyond the initial peaks, remains important. Prior studies have focused on the early phase, leaving out subsequent and updated mortality trends.

pmc-12799439.title: From rare procedure to institutional capability: a proposal to embed systematic training and adoption of emergency front of neck access
pmc-12799439.creator: Caoimhe C. Duffy, Gary A. Bass, Lewis J. Kaplan, Christopher P. Bonafide, Ellen P. O'Sullivan, Paul A. Baker
pmc-12799439.description: SummaryEmergency front-of-neck access (eFONA) usage and performance vary across clinical settings despite its essential role in airway rescue. Therefore, delay or suboptimal execution occurs when eFONA is required for life-saving rescue. This observation may stem from fragmented instruction, lack of systems-level reinforcement, limited opportunities for practice, and rapid skill decay.

pmc-13067184.title: Programmed cell death receptor 1 inhibitors combined with paclitaxel-platinum induction chemotherapy for treating patients with locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a real-world retrospective study
pmc-13067184.creator: Lilan Chen, Xing Song, Junjun Chen, Junchao Huang, Wendong Gu, Wenjie Jiang
pmc-13067184.description: BackgroundConcurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) combined with induction chemotherapy (IC) is the standard first-line treatment for locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC). However, treatment-related toxicities and the risk of recurrence or metastasis remain clinical challenges, which have prompted the development of strategies that can improve efficacy while minimizing adverse effects.

pmc-13293831.title: Children’s privacy, autonomy, and digital identity in sharenting research: a scoping review with bibliometric mapping
pmc-13293831.creator: Osman Akay

pmc-13296757.title: Role of the nonhelical tailpiece of myosin-II in regulating filament architecture and function
pmc-13296757.creator: Kangji Wang, Shi Shu, Xiong Liu, Erfei Bi
pmc-13296757.description: Wang et al. show that deletion of the nonhelical tailpiece (NHT) in myosin-II results in enlarged bipolar filaments with reduced bare zones, decreased disassembly, and impaired cell migration, providing mechanistic insight into disease-associated stop-codon mutations in the NHT of myosin-IIA.

pmc-13350565.title: A Qualitative Comparative Study of the Doctor-Patient Relationship Model and Decision-Making Style among Chinese and Japanese Doctors
pmc-13350565.creator: Hua Xu, Taketoshi Okita, Masao Tabata, Atsushi Asai
pmc-13350565.description: The nature of doctor-patient relationships (DPRs) and decision-making style (DMS) is related to patient satisfaction, clinical outcomes, and the occurrence of disputes. Given the importance of understanding the current state of DPRs, we conducted an exploratory analysis of the current state of DPRs and DMS in clinical settings in China and Japan.

pmc-13451291.title: Push until it breaks: engineering is stronger when we know its limits
pmc-13451291.creator: Unknown
pmc-13451291.description: Engineering and applied science papers too often stop at what succeeds. We ask authors to push their assumptions, methods, models, or devices until they falter, and to report where and why they break. Disclosed limitations are a mark of rigour, not a liability at review: they show the field where the next advance will have to come from.
